We’ll kick things off with a quick word from Jane and our endorsed candidates, followed by a brief training before we hop on the phones. So, whether you’re a seasoned phone banker or a first-timer, this is a great opportunity to support some amazing candidates. In case you’re not familiar with this race yet, here’s a quick recap:
The Port Commission (formally known as the Brownsville Navigation District Commission) makes decisions that directly affect the livelihoods of thousands of South Texans. They get to decide between policies that cater to the biggest corporate polluters and policies that prioritize a liveable future for all of our communities by promoting sustainable and equitable development.
That’s why we’re supporting the three candidates who comprise the Port For All slate:
* **Josette Cruz Hinojosa,** focused on community needs and improving workers' conditions at the Port.
* **Patrick Everitt** , committed to bringing healthier jobs and a cleaner environment to Brownsville.
* **Andres Rios** , who brings invaluable experience, driven by a personal commitment to his family and community.

Your voice can help ensure these candidates have the support they need in the upcoming elections. Can we count on you to join us and make a difference? body:
Will you please join me in supporting my friend Lucas Kunce for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat?
#
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h)
Hey Peter, it’s Jon Hamm, born-and-raised Missourian.
In a moment, I’m going to ask you to **[chip in $10 or whatever you can afford toward my friend Lucas Kunce’s campaign for U.S. Senate in Missouri.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) But first, please give me a moment to explain what my home state is up against in this election and why I’m supporting Lucas.**
**[CHIP IN TO SUPPORT LUCAS KUNCE →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h)**
Most of my family is from a town called Ste. Genevieve. I’ve watched their community go downhill for years.
While corrupt politicians shipped jobs overseas and voted to give handouts to Wall Street and their corporate allies, everyday people just trying to survive in the place they call home ran out of money and opportunities.
**Our leaders abandoned them — and Josh Hawley is the perfect example.**
Instead of fighting for what would make the communities in my home state stronger, Josh Hawley has been busy engaging in out-of-touch culture wars and selling us his book all about “manhood” — telling the whole world that the only way to be a man is to be exactly like him.
Well... when I think about manhood, I think about courage. And that’s not something you can give speeches or write a book about.
Missouri is the Show Me State. Courage is something you have to show us.
**That’s why I’m supporting Lucas Kunce for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.** As a born-and-raised Missourian who joined the Marines to serve the community that took care of him growing up, Lucas has already shown us that he knows the true meaning of courage.
Lucas knows courage is about standing up to the powerful and working to rebuild our state. And he knows real leaders fight to empower everyday people and secure our future for generations to come — not for their own power or profit.
**So Peter, if you want to be told about manhood, some guy wrote a book about it.[But if you want someone to show you real courage, please join me in supporting Lucas Kunce’s campaign for U.S. Senate by chipping in $10 or whatever you can afford today.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h)**
If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:
[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=5&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=6&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Contribute $30](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=30&t=7&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Contribute $50](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=50&t=8&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Contribute $100](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=100&t=9&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Contribute $250](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48217?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=250&t=10&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=11&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h)

**Lucas has been working hard to put Missouri’s Senate race on the map in 2024.** From calling out Josh Hawley’s blatant corruption to building a coalition of working people, national organizations, and local leaders — he is Democrats’ best chance to defeat a GOP incumbent and flip a U.S. Senate seat this election cycle.
He’s building a truly grassroots campaign, without a cent from corporate PACs, to defeat Hawley and take back power for everyday working Missourians — just like my friends and family members all across the state.
**It has never been more important to elect a warrior for working people like Lucas Kunce to the U.S. Senate.[So Peter, will you join me in supporting Lucas’ campaign by chipping in $10 or whatever you can afford today?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/48216?refcode=em20240425-5361&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=12&akid=5361%2E614464%2E6Sz_3h)**

Thanks for standing with me,
Jon Hamm

body:
I am ENRAGED at what I’m seeing in my home state.

| |

---
| | | This is Elise Stefanik.

I am ENRAGED at what I'm seeing in my home state of New York. The Jew-hating, pro-Hamas, violent rioters taking over Columbia University is a national disgrace.

They lit American flags on fire, they blockaded Jewish students from walking in certain areas, they formed a violent mob on campus, and they led pro-terrorist chants.

**The rot in American higher education runs DEEP. **

Late last year, we made history by forcing the presidents of Harvard and MIT to resign... But our job isn't finished. Turn on your TV and see for yourself. _**[That's why I'm recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE - and I respectfully ask you to sign it before the end of the day.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zgnjir7534ar8c0bnv88pr142o1hjcjps4m351ng_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chh69pj4c5h2bs "That’s why I’m recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE – and I respectfully ask you to sign it before the end of the day.")**_
---
| | | [SIGN MY NATIONWIDE PETITION](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z3ll2293hthjujmu4ns88bc8rvdof701ecjgo1f8_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chh69pj4c5h2bs "SIGN MY NATIONWIDE PETITION")
---
Listen, now is not the time for half-measures.

_Personally, I believe every violent student harassing their Jewish peers should be expelled. Every faculty member involved should be fired. And the NYPD should move in to restore order._

But - at the very least - the person in charge of the school who let this violence spiral out of control should RESIGN IN DISGRACE!

I'm partnering with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to collect 1,000,000 signatures by the end of the week. If we can hit that goal, it will send a message that will be IMPOSSIBLE to ignore.

_**[I'm counting on your signature to hit that goal.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcbk0mn8jrn907p2scfigqls0i89di3lac1mnfag_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chh69pj4c5h2bs "I’m counting on your signature to hit that goal.")**_

Thank you,
Elise Stefanik

name: Elise Stefanik
subject: Dear Columbia University President: RESIGN IN DISGRACE!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by TEAM SCALISE, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and to benefit SCALISE FOR CONGRESS and EYE OF THE TIGER PAC
body:
I am ENRAGED at what I’m seeing in my home state.

| |

---
| | | This is Elise Stefanik.

I am ENRAGED at what I'm seeing in my home state of New York. The Jew-hating, pro-Hamas, violent rioters taking over Columbia University is a national disgrace.

They lit American flags on fire, they blockaded Jewish students from walking in certain areas, they formed a violent mob on campus, and they led pro-terrorist chants.

**The rot in American higher education runs DEEP. **

Late last year, we made history by forcing the presidents of Harvard and MIT to resign... But our job isn't finished. Turn on your TV and see for yourself. _**[That's why I'm recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE - and I respectfully ask you to sign it before the end of the day.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z79sc0uj6k7a048iqs8i57h2v0nmcvej6g3dsmvg_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chj68o36cjh2bs "That’s why I’m recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE – and I respectfully ask you to sign it before the end of the day.")**_
---
| | | [SIGN MY NATIONWIDE PETITION](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z79nv7cv9tbidsr74mf88inq4g1fls2k2plhkn18_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chj68o36cjh2bs "SIGN MY NATIONWIDE PETITION")
---
Listen, now is not the time for half-measures.

_Personally, I believe every violent student harassing their Jewish peers should be expelled. Every faculty member involved should be fired. And the NYPD should move in to restore order._

But - at the very least - the person in charge of the school who let this violence spiral out of control should RESIGN IN DISGRACE!

I'm partnering with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to collect 1,000,000 signatures by the end of the week. If we can hit that goal, it will send a message that will be IMPOSSIBLE to ignore.

_**[I'm counting on your signature to hit that goal.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z97138p9htfjjahok751pf0h8r87rvm9u432jtc8_rp22sh2s8i6ep31chj68o36cjh2bs "I’m counting on your signature to hit that goal.")**_

Thank you,
Elise Stefanik

## U.S. Economy Shows Signs of Slowdown
U.S. economic growth [slowed significantly last quarter](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL2K4zAUhZ9G7q6xrhTbKVyEzRq2yE4zMKWR7StbM_oJkhKRtx889VQHzoHDx_dxm27KWOO3_8rRkHWY1JLNkyYJ2ALKSVbroImQREUD77jkQp4lVvtw6mlucD5hv8w96XYhjiT42va6E6jPlRmwQdlIbJv-1Aqs5-XMNfJezMRJdTOTDa0mh1h_BuPzTtq-wpNivQRX2WHP-Z6YuDAcGY6llNolf2wMR_LwSAxHFzy9jlTxi_LRPCABLcEHZxbYYih5h2RDSZADcGjBeG1VNsFDyuqVQJt4PKoIlwv3f7f3mYnx7c-_KxNX5ZNL3lNJnFdxWO_FWGtS2zHZbE4Z-4OafxX3HQAA__8iFm_f), increasing by only 1.6%, well short of expectations and considerably lower than the 3.4% growth rate reported in the final three months of 2023. Consumer spending climbed only 2.5%, [outpaced by an inflation rate](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsj7FugzAQQL_G3kD23QWHwUMXtnTtiDhzgCuDEbhB-fsqnbs96UlPel-P_jHEFLf5c1jFlyn3QyjxKT1V0FRAPenRTyIgqMVbZ8kitQR68SwOJ8Msd8PowACyCRYQb-xaCEFHDwbIEDTmfmsQag6tncDekcXK4FiRkTGWfNTfOW5lkSm98lOOOuRVJ7-Usp8KPxR0CrrruurA5ybX-fYKujcq6OZxr37OSkLe8vpS0OnDj_sVU4pn4xSZeR1i-muWfw9_AwAA__-zQVHg) of 3.7% in the first quarter. Analysts blamed a surge in imports and a buildup of unsold goods at businesses. The poor economic news [wasn't received well by Wall Street](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL2O6yAQRp_G7ohgGEMoKG6TLrfd0uJnSNhgiAxKlLdfeestP33NOefrul5dLrne_ruN7EhtdWHkF63IQDHAFedoExGQnMkKLVBINAjz3VLyhMp4Y0DrRUOQioxWPCKQdtzM2QIH5AiKnxcl4eSDEQnEWXoS5LSfkFPMo-2n75bruFMqn_ai_RTaNhd7H-PZJ_lvgssEF_es9O7HdYx95FBogksfLTzY5vYHjc4-VFmuqbiRW2Xk9prrrbNBvTimNJeokxJx4XyJIRFHcUjw6H0Kcd5tfL5zKbkrPSG_bS6XX5bxZ5mfAAAA___OdGS7). The S&P 500 fell 0.5%, the Dow dropped 375 points, or 1%, and the Nasdaq composite sank 0.6%. It also dampened expectations that the Federal Reserve would cut interest rates at next week's meeting.
## Anti-Israel Protests Spread to 30 Campuses
Anti-Israel protesters have built protest encampments on at least 30 colleges across the country, including campuses in Texas, Massachusetts, Michigan, and California. [Click here for the latest on pro-Palestinian campus protests](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0LFugzAQxvGnMZuRfRwEBg9d2NK1I7LNQVwZG-EjqG9fJerY7S_9lk_f13262xBDWj_tRoaXPFnP4UkTSugk4ITVbBYioKYio28adYMDQvUwSNR2rW3coHBpO9u1FlwDBD0qItVXwYACVAid6tuugdr5QS-g-8aRJntzAhXNgfNRf-eQ-EFL_MlPOmqftyqaB_NeRPMhYBQwXtdVJ-cTXeXlAsZXChjPIv8qhidJF_MqYPQ5npsLVu5HZipc5FvPfbZMkpK3275RYulz4pBOkj7HSCvJRGvmYJmK3OXhk9U4aK2rw8z7FWIMpbsJVOtmQ3wv5X9_-w0AAP__Ru5xsQ). Not all protests were peaceful. Boston's Emerson College canceled Thursday's classes after [more than 100 protestors](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFu8yAURp8GNiJz4SdkYPgXb-na0cJwMVTY1wKaqG9fJXO3T_qkc6TzeV_uvtRybB9-RzcSLT6M8sBFCzAC9KJ5dAkRUHF08iq1VPqmgWdnvfLJ-pSMTDaYZFOIekUVZDJRecOLgwn0pMFM9p9RcFnDTSaQVq0o0V9XpieMZVC7fFE5RsZUf-iB7RJo59XlMc7O1H8GM4N5ZMyl1tfHYM6044HPzmDG-B38KHQwmLWByd5AnEhnReFbwz4wirPReK3WxUm1BBSh-p4F7tg6HSJQrbihWKmPN4g3F89nqbV0c2V62nZf3m4-_qz0GwAA__9oIGwT) were arrested and four police officers injured Wednesday night. At the University of Texas in Austin, state police arrested more than 50 protesters. In Washington D.C., [students and faculty from area colleges](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFuwyAQQL8Gb0TmfAVnYOjiLV07WhjOgQqDZc6J8vdVOnd8esOT3vdtvrmUU7l_uY0sr3V2ntODZpSgJeCMXbArEdDQkVVGoRrwitBFa3qjB6dHf1UU3ODBK0QaMShANOvSJQs9YI-g-_FDD3BZ_FWtoMZhIUXOLAJ7ConrcfmpqXCkNb_qg46Lr1uXbWTemxg-BUwCJo4UU85vJ2CKdaNCzyZgonB6x6kWARNqUGiMDF42PgMVbnJ1_sz8ktmdxUfp67akQkHuR5W7y9Q4FXoTU2N5f54Cpu6wYX-mnFPTRmB_31z6S3f876TfAAAA__-GxGoo) and universities converged on the George Washington University campus for a combined demonstration. Meanwhile, at Columbia University, the so-called epicenter of the student Anti-Israel movement, university officials have given [protesters a Friday deadline](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLFuwyAQQL8Gb0TmfAVnYOjiLV07WhjOgQqDZc6J8vdVOnd8esOT3vdtvrmUU7l_uY0sr3V2ntODZpSgJeCMXbArEdDQkVVGoRrwitBFa3qjB6dHf1UU3ODBK0QaMShANOvSJQs9YI-g-_FDD3BZ_FWtoMZhIUXOLAJ7ConrcfmpqXCkNb_qg46Lr1uXbWTemxg-BUwCJo4UU85vJ2CKdaNCzyZgonB6x6kWARNqUGiMDF42PgMVbnJ1_sz8ktmdxUfp67akQkHuR5W7y9Q4FXoTU2N5f54Cpu6wYX-mnFPTRmB_31z6S3f876TfAAAA__-GxGoo) to vacate or face "alternative options."
## List: A Quirky Fact About Every State
A new list looks at "bizarre but brilliant" [oddities about every state](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0LFyhCAQgOGnwQ4Hlg1qQZHG7tKmdEBWjwwnN7inuTx95lKn_4p__s_LdPEpp2398DdyvJTJz5wOmlCClYATNtEtRECmIac7jdrggNBcnTUQYYlokIztDA2kbIhWDRGUh6ib5EABKgSr-jdroA3zoBfQvQmkyXdBoKKYuNT2q6SNr7TkZzmotnO5Ndldme-7MO8CRgHjeZ5tLgfR9z2Xmrb1pQSMq8-Z6jOnnQWMWvWqRwFjSD--VpLhwTLUlHPyG8vFz7xLH8qDJR1Un_Kxy509U1NdvJ8vt9tOoFpvPuW_EP53y28AAAD__w_xZZ4) in the nation, from Alabama's Unclaimed Baggage store to Wyoming's two -- and only two -- sets of escalators in the entire state. At the University of Texas in Austin, state police arrested more than 50 protesters. **With personal freedoms at stake, it’s critical for us to know where you stand, friend — _we want to hear from you!_**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83744920/469393057/-686989786?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=43614&ask=10&amounts=5,25,50,100&code=jtk4979-su-nd&refcode=jtk4979-su-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYzBmMDA0OC1jNzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hJWupcAb6_XFRLrUP9j_GUzPgHWLeUZjmCPhyxpMCzk=&emci=e4c0e96e-3802-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&emdi=bc0f0048-c703-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ceid=7659029)
The recent state Supreme Court rulings in Florida and Arizona allowing near-total abortion bans are set to take effect soon — which is why defending our pro-choice Senate majority and codifying reproductive freedom nationwide are **more critical now than ever before.**
There’s no doubt about it, friend: **Reproductive rights _will_ be on the ballot in 2024. **

| Dear Peter, As an elected official, climate and environmental issues top my priority list. Every day I seek solutions—at both the systemic and individual level—for a livable world that is more just and inclusive. ******Focus: Increasing Energy Justice by Reducing Energy Burdens** My legislative and daily work strives to put the pieces in place to build a just energy system. The goal is to provide affordable, clean energy to everyone, while also creating energy jobs that build up the middle class. Lowering our “energy burdens” is a big piece of this puzzle. A family’s “energy burden” is defined as what portion of their income is spent on their home energy utility bills—electricity, gas, propane or oil. Do you remember [reading](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83746221/469396286/1387039781?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2JiNWRlMy1jYzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nVloGho6QutSxklG9Im8VzGtXfhtn8I6YXsUw6HVuuM=&emci=a464f271-5b03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&emdi=23bb5de3-cc03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ceid=37927032) that people should not have to pay more than a third of their income on “shelter” expenses? Of that, our “energy burden” shouldn’t be over 6% of income in order for a family to be able to afford their other monthly bills. Some are fortunate enough to rarely think about Pepco and Washington Gas bills. Yet for many in our community, monthly utility bills and the resulting energy burdens are too high, much more than their budgets can handle. Our neighbors are having to decide which bills to pay—electric? food? medicine?—and which ones they can’t. Additionally, while everyone should be doing what they can to lower their energy use by installing more energy-efficient appliances and weatherizing their homes, these options are often financially out of reach for many low-income households. If you want to learn more, I found this [report](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83746244/469396303/1395545736?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2JiNWRlMy1jYzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nVloGho6QutSxklG9Im8VzGtXfhtn8I6YXsUw6HVuuM=&emci=a464f271-5b03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&emdi=23bb5de3-cc03-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ceid=37927032) interesting explaining the energy burden landscape in Maryland. **My Record on Energy Justice**
Since I was elected 6 years ago, I have been working to ensure that every family in Maryland can afford to pay their energy bills. _On a systemic, big-picture level, in Annapolis I have_ :
• fought for jobs that provide a living wage so fewer people are in a position that they are struggling to pay their bills; • sought to bring greater transparency and accountability of our publicly-regulated utilities in an effort to protect ratepayers and ensure our climate goals are met; • required state agencies to streamline the application process for all safety net services—including energy assistance; • passed legislation to coordinate and consolidate a range of federal and state funding for energy efficiency and electrification for low income households to decrease their energy use, while also improving indoor air quality and comfort; • advocated for renters, whose energy burden is felt through higher rents, to receive direct energy assistance. My recent legislation ensures landlords provide the necessary information to renters to access these funds; and • been appointed to a working group with the Department of Human Services to improve the energy assistance programs. _In District 20, I have_ : • hosted, since 2021, four **Power in the Park** outreach fairs to let people know how to save on energy costs. We bring in agencies and groups to help residents learn what’s available while having a fun time. I have also developed materials so this model can be replicated by other legislators throughout Maryland; and • helped people who are having difficulty paying their energy bills receive aid. clean_body: | | Dear Peter, As an elected official, climate and environmental issues top my priority list. Every day I seek solutions—at both the systemic and individual level—for a livable world that is more just and inclusive. ****Focus: Increasing Energy Justice by Reducing Energy Burdens My legislative and daily work strives to put the pieces in place to build a just energy system. The goal is to provide affordable, clean energy to everyone, while also creating energy jobs that build up the middle class. Lowering our “energy burdens” is a big piece of this puzzle. A family’s “energy burden” is defined as what portion of their income is spent on their home energy utility bills—electricity, gas, propane or oil. Do you remember that people should not have to pay more than a third of their income on “shelter” expenses? Of that, our “energy burden” shouldn’t be over 6% of income in order for a family to be able to afford their other monthly bills. Some are fortunate enough to rarely think about Pepco and Washington Gas bills. Yet for many in our community, monthly utility bills and the resulting energy burdens are too high, much more than their budgets can handle. Our neighbors are having to decide which bills to pay—electric? food? medicine?—and which ones they can’t. Additionally, while everyone should be doing what they can to lower their energy use by installing more energy-efficient appliances and weatherizing their homes, these options are often financially out of reach for many low-income households. If you want to learn more, I found this interesting explaining the energy burden landscape in Maryland. My Record on Energy Justice Since I was elected 6 years ago, I have been working to ensure that every family in Maryland can afford to pay their energy bills. On a systemic, big-picture level, in Annapolis I have : • fought for jobs that provide a living wage so fewer people are in a position that they are struggling to pay their bills; • sought to bring greater transparency and accountability of our publicly-regulated utilities in an effort to protect ratepayers and ensure our climate goals are met; • required state agencies to streamline the application process for all safety net services—including energy assistance; • passed legislation to coordinate and consolidate a range of federal and state funding for energy efficiency and electrification for low income households to decrease their energy use, while also improving indoor air quality and comfort; • advocated for renters, whose energy burden is felt through higher rents, to receive direct energy assistance. My recent legislation ensures landlords provide the necessary information to renters to access these funds; and • been appointed to a working group with the Department of Human Services to improve the energy assistance programs. In District 20, I have : • hosted, since 2021, four Power in the Park outreach fairs to let people know how to save on energy costs. We bring in agencies and groups to help residents learn what’s available while having a fun time. | I was raised in the heart of South Memphis, a vibrant community where every street brimmed with life and local commerce. From the fragrant blooms of our neighborhood florist to the bustling aisles of our local grocery stores, and the laughter echoing from the drive-in theater on warm nights, our community was more than a collection of homes; it was a vibrant tapestry of American life. [But not far from where I learned to read and write, shadowed by the very streets where we played, was the Army Defense Depot. In 1995, during a year that should have been filled with joy as I welcomed a new life into this world, my beloved grandmother, whom we dearly called Ma' Dear, passed away from cancer — a sorrow that many in our community would come to know all too well.](https://l5vsmw.fg98.fdske.com/ec/gAAAAABmK64K9TGUyqroVMTyp8QzTSuNya6r7PAtYo0UU7Ul1vLG5PUd0kHXzGQHdfd9lH59RpcM3B2USR-4C5rIykv-YrC-UWjaCw65h9OzFeE3ipnUv4eOPRe7CDQLl6N4OWhcTgDLe-FUOwruse5f4HWe2Kq7a8krcJDVN0SGV1wDh2qLzmeulJcNuBZIQprQXefSIbXHd_1BWk1nVqoblNVPYbeB-ES48ClNMnS4ZXlOkClSq9_VS3bddTC6tndsXIV-RHq2aMWRv2GMKhgL8SK-6OJCcoXD8asLNs-wTRZfGQQXMRu4C8ag8vQWiedhMn4Y0qp2jBZZWGALYDkOWA_ys8kPYJyR3SYkJI94X88QQWb95VkdV5jqMYooTY-mcSyXQirR) The Memphis Army Defense Depot was no ordinary facility. For half a century, it served as a repository for some of the most hazardous substances known to mankind, casting a long shadow of pollution over our community. The consequences were dire: cancer, heart disease, respiratory illnesses, and an unsettling list of other health crises became part of our everyday lives. These were not just statistics; they were our family, our friends, our future. Driven by a need for justice and a passion for environmental integrity, my mother rallied our community, leading a coalition of 2,500 steadfast citizens to demand accountability and change. It was her courage that inspired me to dedicate myself to environmental policy. [Today, I stand before you, ready to bring that same spirit of tenacity and transformation to a broader stage. Our state and our nation deserve leaders who will confront the challenging issues of pollution and environmental degradation head-on.](https://l5vsmw.fg98.fdske.com/ec/gAAAAABmK64Kf0xosdyDuCmU4FYMiOXohyKASdRzBDIt1ja1a_iNip2pQPeQ3m_o-K6qfjv7wZzpuKtI8n81uVsUOavjxB2EAUMq-wRKdFYyNLGXZZaqr9gxBNoLeapglo5i9TFgnOuxbHbIUGquJn2WNtgZEtysosH1LtUjWNkerL-vDKyJPrchdFkhUnHWbjth-oujXUfr0bBHmCYzssAvV2kEDuvxmjIBTWWgojZ2pug7d01cdD5QcQsk2hH58KGsDj4vWPRBPxNkyvmSr0isYWLL-4y-twaraSP37d446a7PupfvHwZjQAkQvn4zpsbDyoeqIv68zAGExrRxmG_nn1Q0y8aD8l25byGQgpfiULOXlWvCN5TJNgMPjvBEYWOHoWj_91My) This is why Freedom Summer remains a beacon of what can be achieved when communities unite for a common cause. In the spirit of the civil rights warriors of CORE, SNCC, NAACP, and COFO, I am running for office to ensure that Tennessee leads the way in sustainable development and environmental justice. As we look towards a brighter, healthier future, we have a chance to foster new jobs and strengthen our infrastructure. But such progress demands bold, visionary leadership — leadership I am committed to providing. [Yet, I cannot do this alone. With your support, we can make a significant impact. We need to raise an additional $8,560 by the end of this month to keep our campaign moving forward. Whether it's $27, $50, $100, or whatever you can afford, your contribution will power our collective voice and affirm our commitment to making real change.](https://l5vsmw.fg98.fdske.com/ec/gAAAAABmK64KzNxqGMgoht2wW-3fLDT8lbK-5o4tPZMTltsK3-NJ3x47rkP_ATJTa3F5FN-_O2m5ew7kCzx7DZb5DEAzfENYlF6WHdye0KgeLrEA7mMEdKRdUsUYGqlv1wG2QeSJ89O61mXAJcITfAwwT8g2QMy1TFrK4BxUgmGYa7FIvkKA4pmz9enb19Yx3gTTmd3long27K8DedTjCUfE-vo04Zg_gdCE-x69RKvwS_ScOjJjaVilBJw6Ty-okig0o1nLYgn7F-7vV4COTmWyIDnTGqcsNku76h0puQXTB0vPJIC3aDNe1raRgxKV-qx2aRNJPI_ApV9HINzfdMnvfJPpwcwLNrOKsBFbBiXjxEw5SEsWGZzcN9fHexDnTOq64E5TCxzI) Join me in this critical journey. clean_body: Driven by a need for justice and a passion for environmental integrity, my mother... | | | | | | | | | Cleaner, Greener, Stronger: Unite for Tennessee 's Future = | Peter | I was raised in the heart of South Memphis, a vibrant community where every street brimmed with life and local commerce. From the fragrant blooms of our neighborhood florist to the bustling aisles of our local grocery stores, and the laughter echoing from the drive-in theater on warm nights, our community was more than a collection of homes; it was a vibrant tapestry of American life. The Memphis Army Defense Depot was no ordinary facility. For half a century, it served as a repository for some of the most hazardous substances known to mankind, casting a long shadow of pollution over our community. The consequences were dire: cancer, heart disease, respiratory illnesses, and an unsettling list of other health crises became part of our everyday lives. These were not just statistics; they were our family, our friends, our future. Driven by a need for justice and a passion for environmental integrity, my mother rallied our community, leading a coalition of 2,500 steadfast citizens to demand accountability and change. It was her courage that inspired me to dedicate myself to environmental policy. This is why Freedom Summer remains a beacon of what can be achieved when communities unite for a common cause. In the spirit of the civil rights warriors of CORE, SNCC, NAACP, and COFO, I am running for office to ensure that Tennessee leads the way in sustainable development and environmental justice. As we look towards a brighter, healthier future, we have a chance to foster new jobs and strengthen our infrastructure. But such progress demands bold, visionary leadership — leadership I am committed to providing. Join me in this critical journey. Your support not only strengthens our campaign but signals a new dawn for our beloved Tennessee. Hi Peter,
Whew– it’s finally over. The 113th Tennessee General Assembly has adjourned. This session, we spent too much time talking about ways the GOP supermajority wants to harm Nashville and Tennesseans at large and not enough time talking about how we can actually use our state’s resources to help make our state a better place.
We could be funding education rather than trying to jam vouchers through. We could be amending laws to allow women to make their own healthcare decisions rather than criminalizing their bodies. And we could be passing red flag laws and other commonsense gun reform rather than opening up our schools for more guns.
Thankfully, I was able to pass some helpful legislation this session, including requiring the Department of Health to publicly report on gun violence and suicides in Tennessee. I also passed a bill making progress on our hopes to expand passenger train service in our state.
I want to keep fighting for you. This November, I will face a strong Republican challenger in what will be the most competitive Senate race in the state. In 2020, I managed to beat my incumbent Republican opponent by less than 4 points. We must hold onto this seat. My opponent has already contributed almost $100,000 to his own campaign for this election cycle. I don’t have deep pockets and corporate mega donors who are going to fund this campaign. Please consider chipping in today, now that our fundraising moratorium has concluded. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/campbellforsenate]
Thank you so much for your support!
Heidi Campbell

Exciting news!
I will be joining experts and activists from around the world to teach a new class on Embracing our Emergency: Thriving in the climate crisis."
[Embracing our Emergency](https://substack.com/redirect/939ff570-9593-4d46-9905-3d0368ec76aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a series on developing practical and useful ideas to address the urgency and fear people feel about our uncertain future in a warming world.
[Click here to save 30% on registration](https://substack.com/redirect/831f9330-2072-4921-b315-fd141d0ba3c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e06de37-ec2d-4448-8ca3-83d28fd7403c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Guests include:
* **Jane Fonda.** Renowned actress, author, and political activist.
* **Bill McKibben.** Founder of 350.org, the first planet-wide, grassroots climate change movement, which has organized twenty thousand rallies around the world.
* **Gail Bradbrook.** Environmental activist and molecular biophysicist who co-founded the environmental social movement Extinction Rebellion. movement
* **Michael Mann**. Presidential Distinguished Professor in the Department of Earth and Environmental Science at the University of Pennsylvania.

[To view the full list of speakers, click here.](https://substack.com/redirect/939ff570-9593-4d46-9905-3d0368ec76aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_**Registration and cost:**_
Use my exclusive[ registration link here](https://substack.com/redirect/831f9330-2072-4921-b315-fd141d0ba3c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to get 30% off the full course.
We won't turn anyone away because of cost: Please let your audience know they can email hello@liminal.news for a full or partial scholarship.
_**Program:**_
Over the five weeks, you will learn from legendary movement builders and courageous thinkers. You will reach a deeper understanding of the current state of the Earth and the global climate justice movement. You will access the practical tools, resources, networks, and visionary ideas you need to make productive, positive changes, right now, in your life and community.
During this regenerative leadership training, you will have the chance to develop your action plan for the next ten years. This will help you flourish and thrive, even if life becomes more difficult for many due to disruptions and shortages.
Most of us know the corporate-controlled mainstream media severely under-reports the reality of the worldwide ecological catastrophe we have unleashed. Most people remain disengaged and detached from what's happening. This is understandable, as it seems overwhelming and out of anyone's control.
Those of us who have the courage to face the situation constitute a vanguard. It is not easy, psychologically. But beyond the pain, there is truth. And in truth, there is power.
This culture has put future generations in peril in its quest for profit and endless unsustainable growth. We all know in our hearts that this system won't continue for too much longer. But we don't know what comes after it. People are unprepared for what is going to happen as we dive deeper into what our speaker Nate Hagens calls the "Great Simplification." By joining EMBRACING OUR EMERGENCY, you will become an early adapter, not only confronting the negatives but also recognizing the new opportunities - for personal fulfillment, creativity, activism, and purpose-driven entrepreneurship - in this unprecedented time.
We have the capacity to find freedom, strength, and even joy in accepting what is, while we define a meaningful, active role for ourselves. Taking a spiritual perspective, we can see this time as a call for planetary initiation and an opportunity for each of us to undertake the archetypal hero's journey.
Despite the huge forces at play, here is still a huge amount you can do for yourself, for your community, and for the Earth. Sometimes, times of crisis are actually the best times. Together, let's embrace this precious opportunity to access our greatest potential.

_**PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE:**_
* Interactive live sessions with legendary movement builders and courageous thinkers on how you can live and lead in a time of climate chaos.
* Online community of people across the world building networks of resilient and regenerative practices
* Special sessions to help emotionally process climate-related emotions with a community of peers
* Option for "homework": Creating your action plan for the future, based on a deep understanding of the underlying dynamics
* Unlimited replays of session recordings and access to resource library
* A portion of proceeds from the course will be donated to multiple climate action organizations, and to the production of Josh Fox's new documentary film The Welcome Table.

Sessions will be held from 1-4pm EDT on Sundays and 2-4pm EDT on Wednesdays.

Apr 26 | | | | | | | | | | | Exciting news! I will be joining experts and activists from around the world to teach a new class on Embracing our Emergency: Thriving in the climate crisis." is a series on developing practical and useful ideas to address the urgency and fear people feel about our uncertain future in a warming world. | | ---|---|--- Guests include: Jane Fonda. Renowned actress, author, and political activist. Bill McKibben. Founder of 350.org, the first planet-wide, grassroots climate change movement, which has organized twenty thousand rallies around the world. Gail Bradbrook. Environmental activist and molecular biophysicist who co-founded the environmental social movement Extinction Rebellion. movement Michael Mann. Presidential Distinguished Professor in the Department of Earth and Environmental Science at the University of Pennsylvania. Registration and cost: Use my exclusive to get 30% off the full course. We won't turn anyone away because of cost: Please let your audience know they can email hello@liminal.news for a full or partial scholarship. Program: Over the five weeks, you will learn from legendary movement builders and courageous thinkers. You will reach a deeper understanding of the current state of the Earth and the global climate justice movement. You will access the practical tools, resources, networks, and visionary ideas you need to make productive, positive changes, right now, in your life and community. During this regenerative leadership training, you will have the chance to develop your action plan for the next ten years. This will help you flourish and thrive, even if life becomes more difficult for many due to disruptions and shortages. Most of us know the corporate-controlled mainstream media severely under-reports the reality of the worldwide ecological catastrophe we have unleashed. Most people remain disengaged and detached from what's happening. This is understandable, as it seems overwhelming and out of anyone's control. Those of us who have the courage to face the situation constitute a vanguard. It is not easy, psychologically. But beyond the pain, there is truth. And in truth, there is power. This culture has put future generations in peril in its quest for profit and endless unsustainable growth. We all know in our hearts that this system won't continue for too much longer. But we don't know what comes after it. People are unprepared for what is going to happen as we dive deeper into what our speaker Nate Hagens calls the "Great Simplification." By joining EMBRACING OUR EMERGENCY, you will become an early adapter, not only confronting the negatives but also recognizing the new opportunities - for personal fulfillment, creativity, activism, and purpose-driven entrepreneurship - in this unprecedented time. We have the capacity to find freedom, strength, and even joy in accepting what is, while we define a meaningful, active role for ourselves. Taking a spiritual perspective, we can see this time as a call for planetary initiation and an opportunity for each of us to undertake the archetypal hero's journey. Despite the huge forces at play, here is still a huge amount you can do for yourself, for your community, and for the Earth. Sometimes, times of crisis are actually the best times. Together, let's embrace this precious opportunity to access our greatest potential. PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE: Interactive live sessions with legendary movement builders and courageous thinkers on how you can live and lead in a time of climate chaos. Online community of people across the world building networks of resilient and regenerative practices Special sessions to help emotionally process climate-related emotions with a community of peers Option for "homework": Creating your action plan for the future, based on a deep understanding of the underlying dynamics Unlimited replays of session recordings and access to resource library A portion of proceeds from the course will be donated to multiple climate action organizations, and to the production of Josh Fox's new documentary film The Welcome Table. Sessions will be held from 1-4pm EDT on Sundays and 2-4pm EDT on Wednesdays. body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=6306%2E5257348%2ECc4Lbu ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Derek, on
Wednesday, the Supreme Court heard yet another abortion case that could
impact access to emergency medical care.

The Biden administration challenged Idaho’s near-total abortion ban in
Moyle v. United States, asserting that federal law supersedes the ban and
requires Medicare-participating hospitals to offer abortion care if
necessary to provide stabilizing treatment.

The Supreme Court’s forthcoming decision could set a dangerous standard.
If Idaho’s ban is allowed to take precedence over the federal Emergency
Medical Treatment and Labor Act, it signals to other states that the Biden
administration’s work to restore abortion access in states with total or
near-total bans can be overturned.

But let’s take a closer look at how we got here,
Derek, because this case isn’t
just about reproductive freedom — it’s also about the reactionary and
compromised nature of the Supreme Court.

I am proud to champion reproductive freedom. In my tenure in Congress, I
have cosponsored the EACH Act, the Women’s Health Protection Act, and the
Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act. I also voted to codify
Roe v. Wade into federal law. But part of this crucial work to defend
abortion rights includes holding our ultra-partisan Supreme Court
accountable.

We wouldn’t be in this position if Senate Republicans hadn’t allowed Trump
to stack the Supreme Court with anti-abortion extremists — including Brett
Kavanaugh, whose history of sexual misconduct should have disqualified him
from this lifetime appointment from day one.

It will take bold but necessary action to reform our judicial system. I
support expanding the Supreme Court and am a lead author of the Judiciary
Act, which would expand the number of justices from 9 to 13. I also
support term limits, an enforceable code of ethics, and banning stock
trading for judges.

By holding the Supreme Court to account, we can make big changes for
abortion,
Derek. A fair, balanced, and
representative Court will be equipped to issue rulings that impact our
fundamental human rights — unlike our current judicial makeup.

How much

Should
individuals be able to accumulate wealth, or should estate taxes
control the amount that can be accumulated and passed on?

What
counts as protected intellectual property?

Questions
like these provoke debates and conflict-not just philosophical or
legal, but political as well- and they have a significant impact
on our daily lives.

The
preservation of property rights depends on a populace committed
to a limited, decentralized government and to respecting the
rights of others. While we have made great progress over the past
fifty years in guaranteeing civil rights, we as a society have
failed to make the connection between civil rights and property
rights.

The
former can only exist if the latter are secure.

shed light on this crucial issue, I would like to offer you a
complimentary digital copy of Property Rights: A Practical Guide
to Freedom and Prosperity. This eBook by Hoover fellows Terry

securing our freedom and promoting our well-being as a society.

Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss has been channeling substantial funds into American state ballot initiatives through the 1630 Fund aka Sixteen Thirty Fund, a progressive advocacy group.As reported by Americans for Public Trust, Wyss’s donations, which total around $243 million to the group, have been instrumental in influencing policies across various states, with a significant focus on Michigan. Since 2017, nearly $34 million has been funneled into Michigan to, among other goals, "rewrite the state’s election laws." This massive infusion of cash aims at bolstering liberal causes from immigration to abortion and enhancing Democratic voter turnout. **Overview of Election Types and Systems** The recent elections comprised various types, including Special Primary, Special General, Regular Primary, and Regular General elections. Each election type presented its own set of rules and systems. Notably, both the Special General Election and the Regular Primary occurred simultaneously. The Special General employed a Top 4 Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) system, whereas the Regular Primary followed a simpler system where voters were to select just one candidate. Complexity of Simultaneous Elections The concurrent scheduling of the Special General Election (using a Top 4 RCV system) and the Regular Primary (select one candidate system) undoubtedly introduced complexities. Voters received a single ballot that included both election types, potentially leading to significant confusion. This complexity was especially pronounced because the instructions for the Regular Primary (to choose one candidate) could easily be mistaken as applicable to the Special General Election as well. Voter Confusion and Election Outcomes The confusion among voters is highlighted by the election outcomes. In the Special General, a Democrat secured victory with 75,000 votes, despite Republican candidates collectively garnering 112,000 votes. This result suggests a significant portion of voters may have followed the Regular Primary’s instructions, opting to vote for only one candidate in the Special General as well. Such a scenario would inadvertently skew the effectiveness of the RCV system, where ranking multiple candidates is crucial. Introduction of Ranked Choice Voting Adding to the electoral confusion was the introduction of Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) for Alaskans. As their first experience with RCV, many voters were unfamiliar with its mechanisms, which require voters to rank candidates by preference. The presence of both a new voting system and dual election types on the same ballot likely contributed to unintended voting behaviors and unexpected election results. Implications and Reflections The overlap of different voting instructions and the debut of RCV evidently had a profound impact on voter behavior and the election’s outcome. This scenario underscores the need for clear communication and voter education, particularly when implementing new voting technologies or systems. Ensuring that voters are well-informed and understand the distinctions between concurrent elections is crucial for the integrity and accuracy of electoral processes.

body:
I am ENRAGED at what I’m seeing in my home state.

| |

---
| | | This is Elise Stefanik.

I am ENRAGED at what I’m seeing in my home state of New York. The Jew-hating, pro-Hamas, violent rioters taking over Columbia University is a national disgrace.

They lit American flags on fire, they blockaded Jewish students from walking in certain areas, they formed a violent mob on campus, and they led pro-terrorist chants.

**The rot in American higher education runs DEEP. **

Late last year, we made history by forcing the presidents of Harvard and MIT to resign... But our job isn’t finished. Turn on your TV and see for yourself. _**[That’s why I’m recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE- and I respectfully ask you to sign it before the end of the day.](https://click.youramerica.news/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=653%7c33585%7c920805%7c0%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=JLjppRC7wz56aRTPQD9Meg&sysid=1 "That’s why I’m
recirculating my nationwide petition calling on the president of Columbia
University to RESIGN IN DISGRACE – and I respectfully ask you to sign it
before the end of the day.")**_

Listen, now is not the time for half-measures.

_Personally, I believe every violent student harassing their Jewish peers should be expelled. Every faculty member involved should be fired. And the NYPD should move in to restore order._

But - at the very least - the person in charge of the school who let this violence spiral out of control should RESIGN IN DISGRACE!

I’m partnering with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to collect 1,000,000 signatures by the end of the week. If we can hit that goal, it will send a message that will be IMPOSSIBLE to ignore.

_**[I’m counting on your signature to hit that goal.](https://click.youramerica.news/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=653%7c33587%7c920805%7c0%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=5PTTN19ljpvUF1MAsTkDRw&sysid=1 "I’m counting on your
signature to hit that goal.")**_

Thank you,
Elise Stefanik

name: Andrea Salinas
subject: 5 reasons for $5
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Andrea Salinas for Oregon
body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83765864/469455049/1744833800?refcode=email_042524_5reasons&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MjE0NDg2NC1lMjAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RYW48SzrEkqQk1n9UTlPpVrCT7h4W1g4TBwk6EOQRoA=) I know I’m probably not the only candidate in this election emailing to ask for your support. (And sorry in advance for adding to your inbox clutter!) To me, that makes it especially important that I take some time to explain why this race, right here in Oregon, is deserving of your time and investment — because I don’t take your support, or anyone else’s, for granted. [_**If you already know that you’re all in on protecting this seat, I’d be honored if you would pitch in $5 and help me win this race (you can click this link to donate)**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83765865/469455050/-554069173?refcode=email_042524_5reasons&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MjE0NDg2NC1lMjAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RYW48SzrEkqQk1n9UTlPpVrCT7h4W1g4TBwk6EOQRoA=). But if you need more convincing, here are five reasons I am humbly asking for your support today: **1) Despite the extreme GOP majority in control of the House, I’ve worked hard to deliver real progress.** In fact, I’m proud to be one of the _only_ representatives — let alone first-term representatives — to pass a new law in this Congress. My legislation ensures that the Grand Ronde Tribe here in Oregon gets land compensation they are owed by the federal government. **2) I’m running proudly on my record of fighting for abortion rights.** Here in Oregon, I helped pass one of the nation’s most comprehensive reproductive rights bills. And now that I’m in Congress, I’m fighting to codify Roe v. Wade protections into law — so that no woman, in any state, can be criminalized simply for making a personal health care decision that some politician somewhere doesn’t like. **3) I know what it’s like when you feel like your family just can’t get ahead.** My dad immigrated to the U.S. from Mexico in 1950 and worked in the fields picking cotton and tomatoes before he was in first grade. He and my mom worked so hard, but when it was time for me to go to college, they didn’t have the money to afford both my education and their groceries. So I put myself through school instead. **4) Today, I’m working to make our economy fairer for families across our country who feel like they don’t have control over their own circumstances.** That means fighting for affordable health care, putting hardworking families over big corporations, and delivering national paid family and medical leave. **5) National Republicans are determined to defeat me — and it took everything we had to fight them off last time around.** This district is one of the most competitive in the whole country. Whichever party wins this seat is likely to win control of Congress, and it’s going to come down to just a handful of votes. To me, that makes it especially important that I take some time to explain why this race, right here in Oregon, is deserving of your time and investment — because I don’t take your support, or anyone else’s, for granted. =. But if you need more convincing, here are five reasons I am humbly asking for your support today: 1) Despite the extreme GOP majority in control of the House, I’ve worked hard to deliver real progress. In fact, I’m proud to be one of the only representatives — let alone first-term representatives — to pass a new law in this Congress. My legislation ensures that the Grand Ronde Tribe here in Oregon gets land compensation they are owed by the federal government. 2) I’m running proudly on my record of fighting for abortion rights. Here in Oregon, I helped pass one of the nation’s most comprehensive reproductive rights bills. And now that I’m in Congress, I’m fighting to codify Roe v. Wade protections into law — so that no woman, in any state, can be criminalized simply for making a personal health care decision that some politician somewhere doesn’t like. 3) I know what it’s like when you feel like your family just can’t get ahead. My dad immigrated to the U.S. from Mexico in 1950 and worked in the fields picking cotton and tomatoes before he was in first grade. He and my mom worked so hard, but when it was time for me to go to college, they didn’t have the money to afford both my education and their groceries. So I put myself through school instead. 4) Today, I’m working to make our economy fairer for families across our country who feel like they don’t have control over their own circumstances. That means fighting for affordable health care, putting hardworking families over big corporations, and delivering national paid family and medical leave. 5) National Republicans are determined to defeat me — and it took everything we had to fight them off last time around. Friends,
Arizona Freedom Caucus Chairman Sen. Jake Hoffman, as well as AZFC member Anthony Kern have been indicted by Democrat Attorney General Kris Mayes.
Their crimes? Supporting President Trump after the 2020 election by presenting themselves as alternate electors while the results of the election were being challenged in court.
This practice has been a part of America's electoral process for decades. [Look no further than](https://substack.com/redirect/586fd60e-e329-4a9c-9efc-2bab7ac6fdc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) President Kennedy's alternative electors in Hawaii while the results were in doubt after the 1960 election.
Yet, political activities such as these have been turned into crimes by political hacks disguised as prosecutors.
Nearly four years after 2020, as Joe Biden seeks re-election, a Democrat AG who won her election by just 250 votes has decided to weaponize her office to target Republican opponents in one of America's most important swing states.
The State Freedom Caucus Network unequivocally stands with our members in Arizona and look forward to a swift acquittal of these bogus charges.
Read more in Sen. Hoffman's [op-Ed for the Daily Wire.](https://substack.com/redirect/afe703d5-4767-43ad-bba2-68d04d3122df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Peter, I grew up across the street from one of Donald Trump's golf courses in New York. This one, in fact: ↘↘ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83767070/469458944/-933762732?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20240426_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTlhMjVlZi1lMzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MCTpjw1P11gkVX12OmA_saL4eNcbdUzJydv6bf5isSM=) Yes, really. But it was not the way I think you're picturing it in your mind — let me explain.

I didn't live in a skyrise apartment or a mansion with luxuries at my fingertips.

**I grew up in the Throggs Neck Houses, a crumbling public housing project among vermin, lead, and mold, across from Trump's Golf Course in The Bronx.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83767071/469458945/-933762732?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20240426_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTlhMjVlZi1lMzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MCTpjw1P11gkVX12OmA_saL4eNcbdUzJydv6bf5isSM=) My mom was a single mom, working multiple jobs to keep food on the table. I'm so grateful for how much she sacrificed to provide for our family.

Living across from Trump's Golf Course, I had to see a reminder every day of how easily and often our government supports and enables the ultra-wealthy at the expense of working families.

You see, the New York City government shoveled over _$100 million in government aid_ to develop this golf course with Donald Trump and the corrupt Trump Organization. _They did this while New York families like mine lived in hunger and poverty across the street._

But, I always try to look at the positives — growing up smelling the stench of Donald Trump (even before he became president) has led me to where I am today: **Fighting in Congress for justice for real working families.**

When I work on legislation, I always think about the families who are struggling just like mine did. I lived that experience — it is not abstract to me. And I'll never forget it.

I hope you feel like you have a better sense of who I am and what my values are. I swear that I'm fighting for those values every day in Congress.

Right now, the shadow of Trump and his MAGA cult looms large. They're determined to strip our right to vote, give tax breaks to people like Trump, and put special interests ahead of working families _– and they’re raising millions to pull it off._

But we have something they don’t, Peter: A powerful grassroots movement made up of working people, not faceless corporations. [**Can I count on you to join our coalition today by chipping in $3 toward our $20,000 end-of-month April goal? If thousands of people like you each chip in what they can afford, I know we can take on their dark money and reclaim our House Majority. »**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83767072/469458946/-933762732?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20240426_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTlhMjVlZi1lMzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MCTpjw1P11gkVX12OmA_saL4eNcbdUzJydv6bf5isSM=) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $3 »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83767082/469458953/-933762732?amount=3&express_lane=true&refcode=RTFC_20240426_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTlhMjVlZi1lMzAzLWVmMTEtOTZmMy03YzFlNTIxYjA3ZjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MCTpjw1P11gkVX12OmA_saL4eNcbdUzJydv6bf5isSM=)

Ritchie Torres represents the future of the Democratic Party. Raised by a single mother in public housing, Ritchie personally understands the hardships that working families endure. At age 25, Ritchie made history as the youngest elected official to serve on the New York City Council. I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class. Peter — I am proud to come from a union family.

I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class, _that’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by six labor unions in St. Louis._

Building a stronger economy starts with fortifying workers' rights and ensuring equity for working Americans. As a former union member (NEA), I understand the importance of standing shoulder-to-shoulder with workers.

In 1967, my grandfather, Reverend Melvin T. Bell, fearlessly spearheaded a strike against Duncan Foundry and Machine Works in Alton, Ill. His leadership resulted in significant improvements in pay and benefits for workers, culminating in a landmark ruling by the National Labor Relations Board.

Fast forward to 2018, amidst the fight against "right-to-work" laws, I took to the streets, knocking on doors to rally support to defeat Proposition A. Together, we stood firm urging voters to say "NO" to measures that threatened workers' rights and fair labor practices. **In Washington, D.C., I will continue to be a strong advocate for workers' rights and a voice that amplifies the need for fair wages and equitable treatment.**

President Joe Biden is making strides at providing good-paying jobs across the nation, and I am committed to advancing these initiatives rather than hindering them. But if I’m going to cross the finish line this November, I’m going to need the support of this grassroots team.

clean_body: Friends, Congresswoman Spartz is proud to announce that her 2024 re-election campaign has been endorsed by the NFIB Federal PAC. Spartz developed legislation and pushed for healthcare transparency and competition reforms in Congress to combat hospital monopolies. In 2022, then Manager of Federal Health Policy at NFIB, Mitch Relfe said, "For over 30 years, NFIB small business owners have identified the cost of health insurance as the number one, long-term small business problem. We appreciate Representative Spartz’s work to address underlying cost drivers of health insurance and increase healthcare competition. We look forward to continuing to work with her on this important effort." "Small businesses have it incredibly tough in today's economic environment," said Rep. Spartz. "From the rising costs of healthcare to increasing inflation and regulations, labor shortages, and skyrocketing taxes, small businesses need people willing to fight for their stability and certainty. Small businesses are the backbone of the American dream, and I am proud to continue being their advocate in Congress." The NFIB Federal PAC is the voice for small businesses, continuously advocating for tax, healthcare, and regulatory reform to legislators in DC. name: David
subject: Understanding Congressional Recess: What It Means for You
body:
This week, the House is officially in recess. While the term "recess" might bring to mind a break or a pause, in Congress, it signifies a vital part | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/davidkimforca/understanding-congressional-recess-what-it-means-for-you?e=fee98d637f)
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friends,

I hope you're having a wonderful week. As part of our ongoing series, "The People's Congress," I want to keep you informed about the rhythms and routines of Congress.
---
| | _**This Week in Congress: Understanding the Recess Period**_

This week, the House is officially in recess. While the term "recess" might bring to mind a break or a pause, in Congress, it signifies a vital part of the legislative duties known as the District Work Period. During this time, there are no votes or official sessions in the Capitol. Instead, Members of Congress return to their home districts. This period is supposed to be dedicated to engaging directly with you, the constituents, and addressing your concerns and needs. However, for Members like Jimmy Gomez, it is a time used for courting wealthy donors and setting up meetings with special interest groups.
---
|
---
| **What Happens During a Congressional Recess?**
1. Constituent Engagement: Members of Congress return to their home districts to engage directly with their constituents through town halls, meetings, and local events. This is a time for them to gather valuable feedback and understand the concerns and needs of the people they represent.

2. Local Oversight: They also monitor the progress of local projects and the implementation of federal policies, ensuring that the community's needs are being effectively met. Are there issues in our district where follow-up is missing? Or have never been addressed? Your representative is supposed to be responsive to the community’s needs.

3. Constituent Services: The local offices remain active, assisting residents with various federal issues such as Social Security, immigration, and veterans' benefits. Were you aware of this potential for assistance?

4. Legislative Planning: What your representative learns from you and other constituents during this period should help guide their priorities and actions once they return to Washington. Recess is a time for reflection and strategic planning, taking into account the voices of the community.

---
|
---
| _**My Commitment to You:**_

While I am not yet a Member of Congress, I am committed to understanding and explaining these processes so that you can better engage with and influence your current and future representatives. Knowing when and how to share your views during these periods can significantly impact the decisions made when Congress is in session.

_**Get Involved:**_

I encourage you to participate in local events and reach out to your representatives during this recess. Your involvement is essential for a responsive and effective government.

Thank you for your engagement and support. Together, we can ensure our community's voice is heard loud and clear in the halls of Congress.

Warm regards,
David Kim
Candidate for Congress, CA-34

Get Involved: I encourage you to participate in local events and reach out to your representatives during this recess. Your involvement is essential for a responsive and effective government. Thank you for your engagement and support. Together, we can ensure our community's voice is heard loud and clear in the halls of Congress. Warm regards, David Kim Candidate for Congress, CA-34 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Copyright © 2024 David Kim for Congress - CA34, All rights reserved.

Peter, **Presently,** **1.6 million American children are enrolled in Catholic schools.** Yet, these vital institutions face an uncertain future because some states prevent parents from directing education tax dollars to their children's school.

That’s a big reason why _**nearly 100 Catholic schools**_ close their doors each year.

**Catholic education is at a crossroads —[and it's imperative we rally together to ensure its survival.](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=34bcf62c64d34390841ea95a8cd8f975&_e=4bZpHLCdJlxMyb9GI5S76VAjwEdEYIAGgaMF4xJBm30EAJbg92goIpkn_cKIbGj64Yqke6Y8DLaAuk4tpIB5_Z3ofM5VnrsMuFGLQEypLYfNbYjqGvCDhA1nicB2AVKju0iwpI_pfCoKbJVC5C9yf7GXPf_hcVdKnRnPzeIlw4wJP2uXq7Fypx2kW5B-q-TNens5WlGx1BWVG6vWMuvLTfQEnRFR0VUmWZ-uH9KJwQ7rGK47mjGLs7P3vCcTfx1Rh_p0t5BeXuGoxMTP9NWDbq1iroeEbJwiuNUYDpC7Yco9Dz-as966pOOHmLoRu1-06Dyi3Ae2ZYaZFNiTK7BWGVKCaqEs2pjdhn2H1LGusprjLh0qf5t4Xh9z1Yy8hEW3E3Ikxb6wbpfBaEmmZO1I4k8S3JQWHxi7BmUepB4tF8GO5w7l7VEB3ubkJXmD4b9r)**

---
[**ADD YOUR NAME: KEEP CATHOLIC SCHOOLS OPEN**](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=34bcf62c64d34390841ea95a8cd8f975&_e=4bZpHLCdJlxMyb9GI5S76VAjwEdEYIAGgaMF4xJBm30EAJbg92goIpkn_cKIbGj64Yqke6Y8DLaAuk4tpIB5_Z3ofM5VnrsMuFGLQEypLYfNbYjqGvCDhA1nicB2AVKju0iwpI_pfCoKbJVC5C9yf7GXPf_hcVdKnRnPzeIlw4wJP2uXq7Fypx2kW5B-q-TNens5WlGx1BWVG6vWMuvLTfQEnRFR0VUmWZ-uH9KJwQ7rGK47mjGLs7P3vCcTfx1Rh_p0t5BeXuGoxMTP9NWDbn4s3dVIJFWm39MrxgE-HnK5xhOJZKJUdxRaJT2XDRDDhR7iQehN4V80PHfWgzFbDnQUi9yhAfGHOtXYD2mtsa_STA_QaElWbxcO5y00rwc5kduv_3nXMZEcZ2UY-1bGmeYVuIc0NOFT0ENUC68tkfn9vbW0wKcBJ935utnZBcF0)
---
This isn't just about losing a cherished American tradition. **It's about __depriving our most vulnerable communities__ of essential educational options. **

**In many instances, these schools represent the ONLY lifeline for families in neighborhoods plagued by underperforming public schools. **

Peter, we believe passionately that these families deserve the freedom to choose, which is why we're staunch advocates for school choice. _**[_**Do you agree?**_](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=34bcf62c64d34390841ea95a8cd8f975&_e=4bZpHLCdJlxMyb9GI5S76VAjwEdEYIAGgaMF4xJBm30EAJbg92goIpkn_cKIbGj64Yqke6Y8DLaAuk4tpIB5_Z3ofM5VnrsMuFGLQEypLYfNbYjqGvCDhA1nicB2AVKju0iwpI_pfCoKbJVC5C9yf7GXPf_hcVdKnRnPzeIlw4wJP2uXq7Fypx2kW5B-q-TNens5WlGx1BWVG6vWMuvLTfQEnRFR0VUmWZ-uH9KJwQ7rGK47mjGLs7P3vCcTfx1Rh_p0t5BeXuGoxMTP9NWDbjclk9o_CuolpzY_4Q3eHrYNR9Ut44pT_ItFxwvKPHOP6CMi6uez5T1-BeJTln0Y4WPlwgjwJaCiHJCzZQQNOUHKCpkwLDr2XUtTmP2IcdtdBa03eeH0coq1Ig4mA4f3AyN8DnQQWfTDmernccedjd-d5-2rBA4rM_ni-fF7VCYK)**_

subject: John Legend, Chrissy Teigen, & Shepard Fairey join me against Big Oil
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC,[janepac
body:
Will you join me, too?

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83769086/469465319/1328794144?refcode=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ms=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxMzlkNDdjLWU2MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=z-gcwIslDiw8QZpM0lm_EO0Upl9vW65m_Hw29pI_R2M=&emci=9e39f08e-d003-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&emdi=c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ceid=4823105)
---
I recently had the honor of joining a great event that brought together some incredible folks in TV, music, art, politics, and activism. While I’d happily find any excuse to catch up with John Legend and Chrissy Teigen, we had a bigger goal in mind: Raising money to stop Big Oil’s attempt to overturn California’s SB1137, the landmark law that shields our communities from harmful oil drilling. [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83769087/469465320/2105508926?refcode=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ms=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxMzlkNDdjLWU2MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=z-gcwIslDiw8QZpM0lm_EO0Upl9vW65m_Hw29pI_R2M=) _**[Click here to read the full story in Politico.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83769088/469465321/-1371297895?refcode=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ms=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxMzlkNDdjLWU2MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=z-gcwIslDiw8QZpM0lm_EO0Upl9vW65m_Hw29pI_R2M=&emci=9e39f08e-d003-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&emdi=c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ceid=4823105)**_ If you haven’t heard about it yet, here’s the gist: California passed a historic bill in 2022 that prohibits new oil wells within 3,200 feet of homes, schools, and other sensitive areas in our communities. It protects our children and families from the harms of close-range oil extraction. Despite _clear_ public support, this legislation is now under threat from the Oil and Gas industry. They've launched a well-funded referendum to repeal this vital law in November, and they’re spending millions to mislead the public into believing these regulations are an overreach. Our event highlighted the disproportionate impact of urban oil wells on low-income communities and communities of color — those who are often overlooked but bear the brunt of environmental injustices. This issue isn't about aesthetics or discomfort; it's about preventing real health hazards like respiratory and neurological diseases linked to proximity to oil wells. Thanks to the overwhelming support we received at the event, we're off to a strong start. But let's be clear: Big Oil and Gas have virtually UNLIMITED sums of money to spend against us to protect their bottom line. So, this fight is far from over. **[Between now and November, Jane PAC will be ramping up our efforts to fight back against the referendum campaign and elect climate champions to the state legislature who will keep up the fight in Sacramento for years to come. Please, make a donation today to support our work.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83769089/469465322/2105508926?refcode=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ms=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxMzlkNDdjLWU2MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=z-gcwIslDiw8QZpM0lm_EO0Upl9vW65m_Hw29pI_R2M=)** **Here's where we need to focus our efforts:**
* **Educational Outreach:** We need resources to inform the public about the dangers associated with nearby oil drilling through mailers, phone calls, social media, emails, texts, and in-person outreach — and in a state as diverse as California, we’ll need to invest in multilingual outreach. Disinformation is a potent tool in Big Oil's arsenal, but truth is more powerful.

* **Legislative Advocacy:** Supporting candidates who champion environmental justice is more crucial than ever. Your **[contributions to the Jane Fonda Climate PAC](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83769090/469465324/2105508926?refcode=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&ms=ea.c139d47c-e603-ef11-96f3-7c1e521b07f9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxMzlkNDdjLWU2MDMtZWYxMS05NmYzLTdjMWU1MjFiMDdmOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=z-gcwIslDiw8QZpM0lm_EO0Upl9vW65m_Hw29pI_R2M=)** will allow us to support more down-ballot candidates who prioritize public health over fossil fuel profits.

* **Community Engagement:** We have to amplify the voices of those directly impacted by oil drilling. While the climate crisis caused by continued reliance on fossil fuels impacts all of us, people in frontline communities are bearing the brunt of these deadly extraction projects. Their stories underscore the urgent need for critical measures like the one CA passed in 2022. clean_body: Will you join me, too? | I recently had the honor of joining a great event that brought together some incredible folks in TV, music, art, politics, and activism. While I’d happily find any excuse to catch up with John Legend and Chrissy Teigen, we had a bigger goal in mind: Raising money to stop Big Oil’s attempt to overturn California’s SB1137, the landmark law that shields our communities from harmful oil drilling. = If you haven’t heard about it yet, here’s the gist: California passed a historic bill in 2022 that prohibits new oil wells within 3,200 feet of homes, schools, and other sensitive areas in our communities. It protects our children and families from the harms of close-range oil extraction. Despite clear public support, this legislation is now under threat from the Oil and Gas industry. They've launched a well-funded referendum to repeal this vital law in November, and they’re spending millions to mislead the public into believing these regulations are an overreach. Our event highlighted the disproportionate impact of urban oil wells on low-income communities and communities of color — those who are often overlooked but bear the brunt of environmental injustices. This issue isn't about aesthetics or discomfort; it's about preventing real health hazards like respiratory and neurological diseases linked to proximity to oil wells. Thanks to the overwhelming support we received at the event, we're off to a strong start. But let's be clear: Big Oil and Gas have virtually UNLIMITED sums of money to spend against us to protect their bottom line. So, this fight is far from over. = Here's where we need to focus our efforts: Educational Outreach: We need resources to inform the public about the dangers associated with nearby oil drilling through mailers, phone calls, social media, emails, texts, and in-person outreach — and in a state as diverse as California, we’ll need to invest in multilingual outreach. Disinformation is a potent tool in Big Oil's arsenal, but truth is more powerful. Legislative Advocacy: Supporting candidates who champion environmental justice is more crucial than ever. Your = will allow us to support more down-ballot candidates who prioritize public health over fossil fuel profits. Community Engagement: We have to amplify the voices of those directly impacted by oil drilling. While the climate crisis caused by continued reliance on fossil fuels impacts all of us, people in frontline communities are bearing the brunt of these deadly extraction projects. Their stories underscore the urgent need for critical measures like the one CA passed in 2022. For first-person stories you can share on social media, We’re gearing up for a November showdown against Big Oil, and every action you take counts. Please, if you've ever felt moved by our cause, let this be the moment you act. Chip in, join us, and let's show the oil industry that their era of unchecked power is over. name: Katie Porter
subject: Deadline for a great program: Every Kid Outdoors will run out of funding if Congress doesn’t act
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Truth to Power PAC
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=38845%2E3422442%2EixnEpD)
Derek,
It’s National Park Week, and I LOVE our country’s National Parks.
Congress has the duty to oversee them, and I’m especially passionate about the Every Kid Outdoors program, which provides fourth graders and their families with free access to National Parks. **I introduced the Every Kid Outdoors Act earlier this year to permanently fund this program—without Congressional action, this program will expire in 2026.**
My bill would permanently fund this program and expand it to fifth grade students. Letting Every Kid Outdoors die would be a huge loss not just for the kids, but for the local economies who rely on park visitors.
This bill is still working its way through Congress, **[can you sign my petition to show your support for fully, permanently funding the Every Kid Outdoors program?](https://act.katieporter.com/signup/ttp-em-parks/?source=em20240426-38845&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&akid=38845%2E3422442%2EixnEpD)**
[Add Your Name](https://act.katieporter.com/signup/ttp-em-parks/?source=em20240426-38845&t=2&akid=38845%2E3422442%2EixnEpD)
Making our parks more accessible allows students to learn about public lands, keeps kids healthy, lets families take affordable vacations, and boosts local economies—a win for everyone. My family has made so many memories at National Parks across the country, and it’s an opportunity everyone should have. Here’s my daughter Betsy and I on our most recent National Park adventure to Pinnacles National Park in Central California.
Wherever you live, I hope you’re able to get outside and enjoy one of our country’s incredible National Parks sometime soon.
Katie Porter
